name: manifest-dev
description: Manifest-driven development: /figure-out reaches shared understanding, /define writes Deliverables with Acceptance Criteria and Global Invariants, and /do implements them until every gate holds on fresh evidence. Each gate is one text — a title, a body, and an optional why — carrying a required kind (judgment or deterministic, never inferred) as its only structured metadata. Re-verification follows that kind: command-backed gates re-run in full, while judgment gates take one full look and then judge only prior findings' repairs and the changed delta. Gate text is immutable to the run and changes only through the skill that authored it. A default-on execution log keyed to the Manifest preserves deviations and dead-end memory across relaunches; --no-log opts out. For unattended runs, /do arms a host-native goal-setting backstop whose completion contract requires fresh evidence for every gate. /auto chains the full flow, and /figure-out-team extends deliberation to multi-party Slack sessions. /ticket-up authors convention-compliant Tickets from a Manifest, direct work, independently managed questions, or source-linked follow-ups; one Manifest becomes one coherent Shaped Ticket by default, with Deliverable splitting reserved for explicit delegation. Follow-up Auto preserves source authority for unattended or nested authoring, while a person at the ticket-up boundary may freshly grant Auto after the new Ticket independently qualifies. /next-ticket claims and presents the ready Ticket whose delay would lose the most project value for the human-plus-AI session, using current executor time rather than traditional feature-size estimates. /run-ticket receives one exact Ticket, recovers its stable branch and pull request, invokes /auto, completes required landing, and records DONE or ESCALATED on that Ticket. /sweep-tickets recovers first or starts one eligible Auto Ticket by the same delay-loss objective per scheduled invocation. Stores use the project's shared tracker, GitHub Issues out of the box, or files where cross-checkout claiming is not needed. figure-out speaks to one reader with limited attention — state at a glance, one slot per set member so a dropped one shows, the ask set apart — with form otherwise its own call. /init-context sets a repository up with the surfaces the workflow reads from — a North Star (the project's standing strategy surface: nine fields from diagnosis to never-does, every position carrying a dated state of evidence, hypothesis, ruled, or empty, informing every session and never binding, with positions changed only by the owner's ruling), project-owned ADR conventions, a glossary, and the context-file wiring that keeps sessions using all of them — seeding them from the project's own history where there is any; re-running it compares the project-owned copies it wrote — forks no sync updates — against the current defaults and offers each difference for the user to take or leave. figure-out's docs mode keeps the North Star current under its update asymmetry and notes when a recorded decision sits outside what the Diagnosis names, since a position also goes stale by drifting out of date while nothing contradicts it, figure-out takes the seat of the person its Who it's for names whenever a read implies making something and enumerates their uses toward their ideal, /define's marketing task file gates outward-facing claims against its Promise and Never, and /next-ticket weighs cross-effort priority against its winning definition. Prose deliverables are gated by register: a shared floor plus one register overlay — documentation (DOCS-STYLE-REFERENCE) or human-voiced writing (WRITING-REFERENCE) — which never compose together, so no deliverable loads two contradictory rules. /review-writing applies the same standards to any text on demand, outside a manifest run. /design supplies standalone design guidance from first principles: the person, the moment they meet the artifact in, and its subject set the feeling, its strength and the visual material. Implementation stays with the invoking workflow; /review-design owns artifact evaluation and its supporting checks.
